descriptions.summary: An unsecured loan to a resident individual for any personal purpose, disbursed to the borrower's own bank account and repaid in equated monthly instalments collected by a recurring mandate, at a rate fixed for the loan's life.
key_features: No collateral: the decision rests on income and credit history
Rate fixed for the loan's life, set by the borrower's credit profile
Equated monthly instalments over 12 to 60 months, collected by mandate
Key Facts Statement with the annual percentage rate before signing
Cooling-off period to exit without penalty
descriptions.long: Mynt reference definition (India), composed of three regulated primitives: the loan itself, a recurring repayment mandate (NACH or UPI AutoPay) the instalments are collected through, and a credit information pull from the credit information companies that feeds underwriting. Sources: RBI Key Facts Statement instructions (2024): a KFS with the annual percentage rate and every charge before the contract is executed; RBI directions on penal charges in loan accounts (effective 1 January 2024): penal charges, not penal interest, never capitalised; RBI Digital Lending Directions: disbursement to and repayment from the borrower's own bank account with no pass-through account, and a cooling-off period of at least three days for loans of seven days or more in which the borrower can exit by repaying principal and proportionate APR without penalty; RBI Fair Practices Code and instructions on recovery: no harassment, calls only between 08:00 and 19:00; the Credit Information Companies (Regulation) Act, 2005: lenders are members of every credit information company and report borrower data; prudential norms: SMA-0 (1-30 days overdue), SMA-1 (31-60), SMA-2 (61-90), non-performing after 90 days. A fixed-rate loan may carry a foreclosure charge (RBI bars them on floating-rate loans to individuals for non-business purposes). ASSUMPTIONS (indicative; each lender sets its own credit policy): ₹50,000 to ₹40 lakh, 12 to 60 months, 10.5% to 24% a year, 2% processing fee, 4% foreclosure charge after 6 instalments, ₹500 penal charge per missed instalment and ₹500 per dishonoured mandate debit, the age, income and credit-score thresholds, 50% fixed-obligation-to-income cap, and the waterfall order. A Mynt reference product names no providers, partners or risk models: the lender that offers it adds its own licence, KYC, credit-bureau and mandate handoffs (with their consent purposes) and its scorecards, governed in its GRC folder. Fees are subject to GST.

core_algorithms.description: Checks identity and income documents for tampering, device and application velocity, and the disbursement account's name against the borrower's before anything is decided.
Knock-outs before the credit decision: age at maturity, recent serious delinquency, written-off or settled accounts, and a credit score below the floor.

core_algorithms.algorithm_name: Personal loan credit decision and sanctioned amount
core_algorithms.description: Grades the applicant on bureau and income data, caps the amount by affordability (fixed obligations including the new EMI within the income cap), the grade and the product maximum, and approves, refers or declines.
Sets the fixed annual rate within the published range by grade, tenor and segment; the KFS shows the result as an annual percentage rate including every fee.
Equated monthly instalment on the reducing balance, broken-period interest to the first EMI date, the full repayment schedule and the annual percentage rate for the Key Facts Statement.
Chooses reminders, mandate re-presentation and contact by days past due and bucket, only through permitted channels and between 08:00 and 19:00.
